title: Review: Angular measures and uniform circular motion; Centripetal force; Simple harmonic motion: definition and graphs; Energy in SHM
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for AQA A-level Physics (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: O01-uk1#t3 term and clue written for the game; C01-1#t4 term and clue written for the game; O01-1#t3 term and clue written for the game; O03-1#t3 term and clue written for the game. Questions: C01-1#N.4a, C02-1#N.4a, O01-1#N.10a, O01-uk1#N.6, O03-1#N.9a, C01-1#N.12a, C02-1#N.3a, O01-1#N.11, O03-1#N.1a, C02-1#N.8b, C02-1#N.15. Some questions repeat from the worlds it reviews.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Isochronous oscillator
items.clue: System whose period does not depend on its amplitude, as in SHM.

items.label: Centripetal acceleration
items.clue: Rate of change of velocity in circular motion, pointing inward, of size v²/r.

items.label: Equilibrium position
items.clue: Place where an oscillating object would rest; the restoring force is zero there.

items.label: Total energy
items.clue: Sum that stays constant for an undamped oscillator: a horizontal line against x.

questions.stem: A bicycle wheel of diameter 0.700 m rotates at a steady rate about a fixed axle, making one complete revolution every 0.250 s. What is the linear speed of a point on the rim of the wheel?

A car travels at constant speed around a bend on a flat horizontal road; its path is part of a horizontal circle. Air resistance is negligible. Which statement about the horizontal forces on the car is correct?

options.text: Friction from the road acts towards the centre and is the resultant force.
Friction acts towards the centre and is balanced by a centrifugal force.
Friction and a separate centripetal force both act towards the centre.
A forward driving force along the bend is the resultant force on the car.

questions.stem: An object in SHM has a maximum speed v_max and a maximum acceleration of magnitude a_max. Which expression gives the period T of the motion?
An object in SHM is released from rest at x = +0.060 m at time t = 0 and oscillates about x = 0 with a period of 1.2 s. What is the object's position at t = 0.20 s?
A mass of 0.25 kg on a spring of spring constant 16 N m⁻¹ oscillates with simple harmonic motion of amplitude 0.050 m. What is its speed when its displacement is 0.030 m?

The drum of a washing machine has a diameter of 0.50 m. It rotates about a horizontal axis at constant speed, with a time period of 0.050 s. What is the centripetal acceleration of a sock pressed against the inside of the drum?
A cyclist rides around a flat circular track at a constant speed of 8.0 m s⁻¹. Which statement about her motion is correct?

options.text: Her velocity is constant, so the resultant force acting on her is zero.
Her velocity changes, so a resultant force acts towards the centre.
A resultant force acts on her outwards, away from the centre of the track.
A resultant force acts on her forwards, along her direction of motion.

questions.stem: A pendulum bob swings to and fro in a small arc. At the lowest point of its swing, what are its acceleration along its path and its speed?

options.text: Acceleration along the path greatest; speed zero.
Acceleration along the path zero; speed greatest.
Acceleration along the path zero; speed also zero.
Acceleration along the path greatest; speed greatest.

questions.explanation: The lowest point is equilibrium: the restoring force along the path is zero there. The bob sped up all the way down and starts to slow on the way up, so its speed is greatest here.

questions.stem: A mass on a horizontal spring moves with simple harmonic motion on a frictionless surface; air resistance is negligible. Which statement about the energy of the oscillator is correct?

options.text: At each extreme, E_k is greatest, because the acceleration of the mass is greatest there.
At each extreme, the total energy is zero, because the mass is not moving there.
At each extreme, all the energy is stored in the spring, because the mass is at rest.
The total energy falls during each cycle, because energy is used up in keeping the mass moving.

questions.stem: A ball of mass 0.20 kg on a string of length 0.50 m is whirled in a vertical circle. At the top of the circle its speed is 3.0 m s⁻¹. Take g = 9.81 m s⁻². What is the tension in the string at the top?
questions.explanation: At the top both forces point to the centre: T + mg = mv²/r. T = 0.20 × 3.0²/0.50 − 0.20 × 9.81 = 3.6 − 1.96 = 1.6 N.

questions.stem: A car drives at constant speed over the top of a rounded hill in the road. Near the top, the road's vertical cross-section is a circular arc. The car stays in contact with the road. At the top, how does the normal force from the road compare with the car's weight?

options.text: It equals the weight, since at the top the car moves neither up nor down.
It is greater than the weight, as when the car drives through a dip.
It is less than the weight, so the forces on it add to a downward force.
It equals the weight plus mv²/r, to balance an outward force.

questions.explanation: The centre of the arc is below the car, so the forces must add up to mv²/r downwards: weight − normal force = mv²/r. The normal force is less than the weight by mv²/r.
